There are many ALT-related concepts. The clinical question "ALT measured at least once" is best served by counting patients with any descendant of the general ALT measurement concept. The cleanest approach uses `concept_ancestor` to capture all standard ALT measurement concepts under "Alanine aminotransferase measurement" (4146380), then counts distinct persons in `measurement`.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT m.person_id) AS n_patients
FROM omop.measurement m
WHERE m.measurement_concept_id IN (
  SELECT ca.descendant_concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 4146380
)

**643,426 patients** have had an ALT (alanine aminotransferase) measured at least once.

This counts distinct `person_id`s in the `measurement` table whose measurement concept falls under "Alanine aminotransferase measurement" (concept 4146380) via the OMOP `concept_ancestor` hierarchy — capturing all ALT variants (serum/plasma, with/without P-5'-P, body fluids, etc.).
